primary_live_page.confirms: This IS the real, live Operations registry page per task brief, backed by GET /api/ops/operators and /api/ops/operators/summary.

phase_a_existing_ui_trace.route_layer: src/ops/operator_routes.py (operator_bp) is THE live Operations registry route layer, confirmed by direct code read -- NOT src/core/operation_dashboard_routes.py, which is a different, older wt_ops_v2-backed dashboard left untouched.

service_layer.OperatorReader: src/ops/operator_reader.py -- read path for list/summary/detail; queries operators, operator_entities, operator_evidence, operator_reviews, operator_identity_state tables in database/wt_ops_v2.db (OPS_DB_PATH).
service_layer.OperatorResolver: src/ops/operator_resolver.py -- resolver run (write path, POST /resolve only).
service_layer.PromotionService: src/ops/promotion_service.py -- reads OPS_DB_PATH + DB_PATH (main DB), used for candidate->canonical promotion decisions.
service_layer.EmergingOperatorService: src/ops/emerging_operator_service.py -- computes candidate/emerging populations, contains the canonical-family 'absorption' block (_compose(), lines ~585-619) gated by canonical_merge_contract.py.
service_layer.OperatorIdentityGovernanceService: src/ops/operator_identity_governance.py -- identity lifecycle: expand/activity/review/resolve/retire/merge/split, all POST-only, human-invoked.
service_layer.InvestigationLifecycleService: src/ops/investigation_lifecycle.py -- DISMISSED/REOPENED workflow over wt_investigation_lifecycle table, keyed by family_id (discovery-side identifier), with full audit trail in wt_investigation_lifecycle_audit.
service_layer.CanonicalMergeContract: src/ops/canonical_merge_contract.py -- gates automatic absorption; requires wallet overlap computed symmetrically across ALL wallet-role fields (not just member_wallets) AND >=2 independent identity-class evidence signals. Directly documents why B48k/Dv34 currently escapes WATCHTOWER absorption (their one shared wallet, EFKV, is recorded in `treasuries` on both sides, and the pre-fix candidate-side check only looked at member_wallets).

db_model.registry_db: database/wt_ops_v2.db (OPS_DB_PATH) -- operators, operator_entities, operator_evidence, operator_reviews, operator_identity_state, operator_identity_events/merges/splits, operator_promotion_reviews, wt_investigation_lifecycle(+audit), wt_operation_candidates, wt_operation_family_confirmations.
db_model.main_history_db: database/flex_complete_database.db (DB_PATH) -- creator_funders and all historical relationship/launch/token data. Never migrated or physically merged into wt_ops_v2.db.
db_model.discovery_corpus_db: database/local_operation_discovery_corpus.db -- candidate_families (385 rows), composite_families (14 rows), direct_funding_edges, upstream_edges, candidate_family_members. Precomputed local artifact, separate SQLite file, read independently.
db_model.cross_db_policy: All three DBs are read independently in Python (sqlite3 connect per-file, mode=ro where safe) and merged in-memory. No ATTACH DATABASE, no cross-db write transaction, per Phase N requirement.

phase_a_existing_ui_trace.operation_state_model: operators.status column, one of OPERATOR_STATES (operator_model.py): CANDIDATE, REVIEW_CANDIDATE, PROVISIONAL, CONFIRMED, REJECTED, MERGE_REVIEW, SPLIT_REVIEW, REVIEW, MERGED, SPLIT, RETIRED.
phase_a_existing_ui_trace.investigation_state_model: Separate, family_id-keyed table wt_investigation_lifecycle: state in (DISMISSED, REOPENED), independent of operators.status -- this is the analyst dismissal/reopen workflow layered on top of discovery-side families, not a duplicate of operator status.
phase_a_existing_ui_trace.analyst_queue_logic: InvestigationLifecycleService (dismiss/reopen with reason codes SPAM_DUSTING/KNOWN_BENIGN/FALSE_POSITIVE/DUPLICATE/SHARED_INFRASTRUCTURE/ANALYST_DECISION/OTHER) plus OperatorIdentityGovernanceService review/resolve/retire/merge/split actions on confirmed operator_id records. Both are human-invoked POST endpoints; no automatic promotion path exists for either.
phase_a_existing_ui_trace.promotion_review_actions: POST /api/ops/operators/<id>/review (operator-level, record analyst decision); POST /api/ops/operators/resolve (trigger resolver run); identity sub-routes for expand/activity/review/resolve/retire/merge/split, all requiring analyst + reason metadata per canonical_merge_contract.py.
phase_a_existing_ui_trace.filtering_search: GET /api/ops/operators/search; GET /api/ops/operators?include_rejected=<bool>&limit=<n> (list_operators excludes REJECTED by default, cap 500).
phase_a_existing_ui_trace.detail_profile_source: OperatorReader.fetch_operator(): SELECT * FROM operators, joined in-Python with operator_entities (ORDER BY evidence_count DESC), operator_evidence, operator_reviews, operator_promotion_history. Launch/creator/provisioning-client/treasury counts derive from operator_entities.entity_type breakdown (TREASURY/CLIENT/CREATOR/etc.), not from a separate launch table -- entity_type is the canonical role tag on each member wallet.
phase_a_existing_ui_trace.evidence_history_tabs: operator_evidence (evidence_type/category/details JSON, ordered by created_at DESC) and operator_reviews (analyst review timeline) are the existing History/Evidence source; append-only, never overwritten.

phase_b_authority_model.principle: operators.status is the ONLY canonical authority state. Everything else is workflow/UI/lifecycle overlay.

investigation_workflow_states.source: wt_investigation_lifecycle table (src/ops/investigation_lifecycle.py), family_id-keyed, structurally separate from operators.status.

ui_filter_only_lifecycle_states.source: activity_status from operator_identity_governance.read_identity_lifecycle(); recomputed from activity timestamps, never overwrites operators.status.

descriptive_non_enum_terms.UNRESOLVED: No literal enum value exists; maps to CANDIDATE/REVIEW_CANDIDATE or null-operator_id (investigation-workflow, not canonical).
descriptive_non_enum_terms.INFRASTRUCTURE: Not an operator status; an entity-role tag (entity_type / NON-ATTRIBUTIVE INFRASTRUCTURE marking on CEX/relay member wallets), UI-annotation-only.

classification.CANDIDATE / REVIEW_CANDIDATE / PROVISION: investigation-workflow-state -- pre-authority, machine/pipeline-populated, freely re-computable by resolver runs until a human acts.
classification.REVIEW / MERGE_REVIEW / SPLIT_REVIEW: investigation-workflow-state -- pending-human-action markers; part of HUMAN_DECIDED once entered (not auto-overwritten) but not yet a terminal authority outcome.
classification.ACTIVE / DORMANT / QUIET / REACTIVATED: UI-filter-only / lifecycle-state -- activity_status overlay, never changes operators.status.
classification.DISMISSED: investigation-workflow-state, scoped to wt_investigation_lifecycle (family_id, discovery-side), fully separate table from operators.status.
classification.UNRESOLVED: descriptive term, not a literal enum -- maps to investigation-workflow-state (CANDIDATE/REVIEW_CANDIDATE or null-operator_id).
classification.INFRASTRUCTURE: not a status; entity-role tag, UI-annotation-only, never a canonical operation state.

phase_b_authority_model.safety_rule_for_this_milestone: New evidence-qualification states introduced by this read model (e.g. HIGH/LOW discovery confidence, RAW_VERIFIED/NOT_PERFORMED/CONTRADICTED) are explicitly EVIDENCE QUALIFICATION -- never written to operators.status and never treated as a canonical-authority-state. They are presentation-layer annotations only.

phase_c_unified_read_model_spec.purpose: One conceptual read-only projection per investigation (operator_id if canonical/candidate, or a discovery family_id/entity if pre-candidate), assembled by joining the 3 stores in-Python. No new tables, no schema change. Implementable as a single Python function (design-only in this milestone -- see implementation_result artifact for why Phase P is not code-shipped).
phase_c_unified_read_model_spec.conflict_presentation_rule: The read model never silently picks a winner between conflicting sources (e.g. historical relationship YES vs raw verification CONTRADICTED, or main-DB YES vs discovery-corpus LOW): both values are always rendered side by side with their own provenance label, e.g. 'Historical relationship: YES / Evidence qualification: LOW / Raw verification: NOT PERFORMED'.

phase_l_watchtower_control.result: CONFIRMED (display_name=WATCHTOWER, operator_id=04265d9f-6eb2-568c-a49e-9253091a4dbb, confidence=CERTAIN, 69 entities). Verified via read-only SELECT queries only (mode=ro URI connections); OperatorReader.fetch_operator() code path traced but not invoked against a live write path; no POST route called.
phase_l_watchtower_control.narrative: CONFIRMED status preserved untouched. Read model in Phase C is additive-only for CONFIRMED operators: historical/evidence/discovery sections become secondary context, canonical status/entity membership remain primary and are never recomputed from discovery-corpus data for a CONFIRMED operator.
phase_l_watchtower_control.cex_lineage: Preserved -- CEX/infra-hop fields (root_cex_infra_category, cex_infra_hop_distance, attribution_state) are additive columns already in candidate_families schema and are surfaced, not removed, wherever present for WATCHTOWER-linked families.

phase_m_3sw2_control.how_identified: Same operators table query: operator_id 64527dc2-8073-50c0-8bd7-7ef49e62d875, display_name='3SW2', status='CONFIRMED', confidence='CERTAIN', summary='Canonical operator promoted from 3SW2 Family by explicit analyst approval.'
phase_m_3sw2_control.result: CONFIRMED (display_name=3SW2, operator_id=64527dc2-8073-50c0-8bd7-7ef49e62d875, confidence=CERTAIN, 1 entity). CONFIRMED status preserved untouched. Same additive-only rule as WATCHTOWER applies; a single-entity confirmed operator is a valid canonical state and the read model does not require a minimum entity count to respect CONFIRMED status.

phase_t_long_term_architecture_principle.statement: ONE operations intelligence workflow, ONE registry (src/ops/operator_routes.py + operators table), ONE investigation workflow (InvestigationLifecycleService + OperatorIdentityGovernanceService), ONE review authority (human-invoked POST endpoints, HUMAN_DECIDED status set), ONE canonical operation state (operators.status) -- backed by MULTIPLE specialized evidence stores underneath: main DB (flex_complete_database.db, historical relationships), discovery corpus (local_operation_discovery_corpus.db, candidate families), CEX mapping (infra_mapping.py / operation_dashboard_routes.py cex-funding-intelligence), and raw-verification ledgers (of_dv34_p1_* artifacts). This is never described or implemented as two independent operation systems; the older operation_dashboard_routes.py dashboard is a separate, narrower CEX/token view that should be LINKED to from Operations, not merged or duplicated into it (see Phase I).

Assumed 'INFRASTRUCTURE' in the task's list refers to the NON-ATTRIBUTIVE INFRASTRUCTURE entity-role marking (CEX/relay nodes), not a status value, since no such operators.status value exists.
Confirmed operator_id for WATCHTOWER and 3SW2 by querying the live DB rather than guessing from documentation, per Phase L instruction to 'first find how Watchtower appears in this registry'.
